card.name: "Potentially" before organ-toxic drug terms
card.fires_on: The word "potentially" (or a linking "and/or") right before an organ-toxicity word like nephrotoxic, hepatotoxic or neurotoxic. It is usually found after "other" in warnings about combining drugs.

modes.label: Potentially before -toxic
modes.description: "Potentially" after "other" or "is", just ahead of a word like nephrotoxic or hepatotoxic.
modes.example: As with other aminoglycosides, gentamicin sulfate is<< potentially>> nephrotoxic.

modes.label: Linking word in toxic lists
modes.example: including paromomycin and other potentially nephrotoxic<< and>>/or neurotoxic drugs such as bac

card.writes: It pushes the model to continue with organ-toxicity word beginnings such as neph, hepat, neuro, cyt and hem.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a warning is about to name a drug as harmful to the kidney, liver or nerves.
